trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
The line must go up: right is number 8, which comes later.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
I can't rule out left or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Going left would leave both number 5 and cell (3,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (left from cell (3,3)) was wrong, so the line must go up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going left would force the line onto number 4 before its turn. So the line goes up.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (6,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
